problem: Which root(s) of the polynomial $p(x)={x}^{3}-5{x}^{2}-25x+125$ have multiplicity $2?$

feedback.problem: Which root(s) of the polynomial $p(x)=27{x}^{3}+9{x}^{2}-3x-1$ have multiplicity $1?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to factor the polynomial. For this polynomial, we can factor by grouping:

$$
\begin{aligned}p(x) & =27{x}^{3}+9{x}^{2}-3x-1 \\  & =9{x}^{2}(3x+1)-(3x+1) \\  & =(9{x}^{2}-1)(3x+1) \\  & =(3x-1)(3x+1)(3x+1) \\  & =(3x-1)(3x+1{)}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the roots and their multiplicities, we look at the factors:

- The factor $(3x+1)$ has an exponent of $2$ in the factored form of $p(x).$ So the root $x=-\frac{1}{3}$ has multiplicity $2.$

- The factor $(3x-1)$ has an exponent of $1$ in the factored form of $p(x).$ So the root $x=\frac{1}{3}$ has multiplicity $1.$

In conclusion, only the root $x=\frac{1}{3}$ has multiplicity $1.$
